work.abstract_text: Extending the spectral bounds of Sun, Luo and Ye [Mathematics of Operations Research 45, 233–271 (2020)], we refute the arbitrary-rank interpretation of the pointer-product conjecture of Abbott, Silva, Wechs, Brunner and Branciard [Quantum 3, 194 (2019), Section 4, p. 5, after equation (26); arXiv:1805.09364v3]. Three orthogonal projections on C^3 give the normalized weak-limit pointer product -1/6 < -1/8. For n measurements in unrestricted finite dimension, the exact minimum is -c_n, where c_1=0 and c_(n+1)=(1+c_n)^2/[8(1-c_n)]. Codimension-one projections attain every finite-length minimum, and c_n increases to 1/3. Thus pointer products have infimum -1/3, separated by 2/3 from the limiting ordered weak value -1. The same bounds hold as envelopes at every finite coupling strength for independent centered Gaussian pointers.

work.title: Extending Sun–Luo–Ye bounds to refute Abbott et al.'s pointer-product conjecture
